# Getting Started with Positron

> **Prompt 1:** Download and install Positron. As you watch the videos in Step 1 and Step 3, follow the activities in the videos and become familiar with Positron.

Since I have used Positron before, I already knew that it was a useful alternative to RStudio. I like its modern interface and how the editor, console, variables, plots, and files are organized. The Data Explorer also makes it easier to examine and filter data visually.

I still feel more comfortable using RStudio because I have more experience with it. However, Positron feels more flexible because it supports R, Python, Git, and AI tools in one workspace. I also find it convenient when I am travelling or when RStudio is not working properly.

::: {.callout-note}
**My first impression:** Positron combines familiar RStudio features with a more modern workspace for R and Python and is also a convenient alternative to RStudio.
:::
# Reflection on AI-Powered Data Science

> **Prompt 3:** In Step 4, the video demonstrates how you can use AI inside Positron.
>
> 1. Describe the different ways AI can be used inside Positron. Some options are free, while others are paid.
> 2. Which AI tools have you installed or set up? Which tools did you find beneficial?
> 3. Apply for GitHub Copilot through GitHub Education, provide a screenshot showing your acceptance, and explain whether you found Copilot helpful or distracting.

## Ways I Can Use AI in Positron

The video showed me that AI can support several parts of a data-science project. Posit Assistant can explain code, generate new code, identify errors, and suggest corrections. Inline suggestions can complete code while I am typing, and Databot can explore data, create summaries, generate visualizations, and help organize findings for a report.

I like that the AI tools work within the coding environment because I do not have to continuously switch between Positron and another website. However, I would still review the generated code because AI suggestions are not always correct.

## AI Tools I Have Used or Set Up

I already use ChatGPT and Claude outside Positron for brainstorming, understanding errors, and explaining code. For this activity, I connected my GitHub account and applied for GitHub Education so I could receive student access to GitHub Copilot.

The most beneficial features for me are debugging assistance and inline code suggestions. Debugging can save time when I cannot understand an error, while inline suggestions can help me remember unfamiliar R or Python syntax. I have not connected a paid API provider because I would prefer to begin with the student tools available without an additional cost.

## GitHub Education and Copilot

My GitHub Education application was approved, as shown in screenshot @fig-github-education. At the time of writing, GitHub was still activating my education benefits and stated that the process could take up to 72 hours.

![GitHub Education approval showing my verified student status.](github-education-acceptance.png){#fig-github-education width=80%}

I have already used GitHub Copilot with R through Visual Studio Code. It has helped me complete commands, remember functions, identify errors, and generate suggestions when I was unsure how to continue my code.

I find GitHub Copilot especially beneficial because its suggestions appear directly inside the code editor. This allows me to receive help without continuously switching between my code and another website.

::: {.callout-note}
**★:** AI for me is most useful when it supports my thinking and learning instead of replacing them.

:::
